description.en: Name the days of the week, talk about the time of day and describe your daily routine with the present tense.
description.so: Magacaw maalmaha toddobaadka, ka hadal waqtiyada maalinta oo sharax nidaamkaaga maalinlaha ah adigoo isticmaalaya waqtiga joogga ah.

body.en: The Swahili week starts on Saturday. Jumamosi is 'day one' after Friday, Jumapili 'day two', Jumatatu 'day three', Jumanne 'day four' and Jumatano 'day five'. Alhamisi and Ijumaa come from Arabic, just like Somali Khamiis and Jimce. You don't need a word for 'on': Jumatatu naenda kazini means 'On Monday I go to work'.
body.so: Toddobaadka Sawaaxiligu wuxuu ka bilaabmaa Sabtida. Jumamosi waa 'maalinta koowaad' Jimcaha kadib, Jumapili 'maalinta labaad', Jumatatu 'maalinta saddexaad', Jumanne 'maalinta afraad', Jumatano-na 'maalinta shanaad'. Alhamisi iyo Ijumaa waxay ka yimaadeen Carabiga, sida Khamiis iyo Jimce ee Soomaaliga. Uma baahnid eray u dhigma 'on': Jumatatu naenda kazini waxay ka dhigan tahay 'Isniinta shaqada ayaan aadaa'.

examples.en: On Friday I go to the mosque.

body.en: A Swahili verb is built from pieces: who + when + action. The piece -na- means now or usually: ni + na + soma = ninasoma (I read / I'm reading). In everyday speech Kenyans shorten ni-na- to na-: naenda, nasoma, naamka. Both forms are correct; the full form is more common in writing.
body.so: Falka Sawaaxiliga wuxuu ka samaysan yahay qaybo: cidda + goorta + ficilka. Qaybta -na- waxay ka dhigan tahay hadda ama caadiyan: ni + na + soma = ninasoma (waan akhriyaa / waan akhrinayaa). Hadalka maalinlaha ah Kenyaanku ni-na- waxay u gaabiyaan na-: naenda, nasoma, naamka. Labada qaabba waa sax; qaabka buuxa ayaa qoraalka ku badan.

title.en: Who is doing it? Subject prefixes

body.en: The first piece tells you who: ni- (I), u- (you), a- (he or she), tu- (we), m- (you all), wa- (they). So: ninakula (I eat), unakula (you eat), anakula (he or she eats), tunakula (we eat), mnakula (you all eat), wanakula (they eat). Swahili has no separate he and she: anakula covers both.
body.so: Qaybta koowaad waxay kuu sheegaysaa cidda: ni- (aniga), u- (adiga), a- (isaga ama iyada), tu- (annaga), m- (idinka), wa- (iyaga). Sidaas: ninakula (waan cunaa), unakula (waad cuntaa), anakula (wuu cunaa ama way cuntaa), tunakula (waan cunnaa), mnakula (waad cuntaan), wanakula (way cunaan). Sawaaxiligu ma kala saaro isaga iyo iyada: anakula labadaba wuu qabsadaa.

examples.en: He or she goes to school.
examples.so: Iskuulka ayuu aadaa ama ayay aaddaa.

body.en: Very short verbs like kula (to eat) and kunywa (to drink) keep their ku- in the present: ninakula or nakula (I eat), ninakunywa or nakunywa (I drink). To say what you don't do, start with si- and end with -i: sifanyi kazi (I don't work), siendi (I'm not going), sili (I don't eat).
body.so: Falalka aadka u gaagaaban sida kula (cunid) iyo kunywa (cabid) waxay ku haystaan ku- waqtiga joogga: ninakula ama nakula (waan cunaa), ninakunywa ama nakunywa (waan cabbaa). Si aad u sheegto waxaadan samayn, ku bilow si- oo ku dhammee -i: sifanyi kazi (ma shaqeeyo), siendi (ma socdo), sili (ma cuno).

body.en: Asubuhi is morning, mchana the middle of the day, jioni evening and usiku night. Remember Swahili time from the numbers unit: the clock starts at 6 a.m., so saa moja asubuhi is 7 a.m. and saa nne usiku is 10 p.m.
body.so: Asubuhi waa subax, mchana waa duhurka iyo galabta hore, jioni waa fiid, usiku-na waa habeen. Xusuuso waqtiga Sawaaxiliga ee cutubka tirooyinka: saacaddu waxay ka bilaabataa 6-da subaxnimo, sidaas darteed saa moja asubuhi waa 7-da subaxnimo, saa nne usiku-na waa 10-ka habeennimo.

examples.sw: Naamka saa kumi na mbili asubuhi.

examples.en: I go to bed at 10 p.m.

note.en: The first day of the Swahili week. Sheng: Sato.
note.so: Maalinta koowaad ee toddobaadka Sawaaxiliga. Sheng: Sato.

note.en: Also the time of the dawn prayer.
note.so: Sidoo kale waa waqtiga salaadda subax.

note.en: Roughly from midday to about 4 p.m. Also 'daytime' as opposed to night.
note.so: Qiyaastii duhurka ilaa 4-ta galabnimo. Sidoo kale 'maalinta' marka loo eego habeenka.

note.en: Mswaki is a toothbrush; originally a chewing stick, like the Somali caday.
note.so: Mswaki waa burushka ilkaha; asal ahaan waa caday, sida Soomaaliga.

note.en: Kunywa keeps its ku-: nakunywa, not nanywa.
note.so: Kunywa waxay haysaa ku-: nakunywa, ma aha nanywa.

note.en: Many Kenyans simply say lunch and supper. Supper is chakula cha jioni.
note.so: Kenyaan badan waxay iska yiraahdaan lunch iyo supper. Casho waa chakula cha jioni.
